title: Choose StormCard's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Hurricane Tracking Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Hurricane Tracking Chart
options.lineage: The newspaper / grocery-bag hurricane tracking chart Miami families tape to the fridge every season
options.thesis: Her card is her own tracking chart: the storm's world, plotted around her house.
options.viewport: Phone. Top: language switch (KRE · ES · EN) and the StormCard mark. Hero: a giant zone plate, 'Zòn B', set like the chart's legend band, with one line 'not your flood-insurance zone'. Below: a tracking-chart grid panel with HER HOUSE plotted and three shelters plotted as numbered markers with miles. Primary action: 'Kote pou m ale' (Where to go) full-width button.
options.risk: Can read as a weather-TV graphic if the grid becomes decoration instead of her real location and shelters.

raised.raise: Total contrast commitment: text is pure navy on paper or pure white on navy, never grey.
Two type sizes only on each screen, both large; rank is carried by weight, case and reversal.
Routes from her house to each shelter drawn only at 0/45/90 degrees on the chart.
States are printed marks: toggles are hollow at rest, filled when on, struck when unavailable.
Every card section carries a small header tab (What this means / Where to go / What to bring / What to do now) with a strict hairline border system.

options.label: Evacuation Route Signage
options.lineage: Florida's blue-and-white Hurricane Evacuation Route road signs and county zone placards
options.thesis: StormCard speaks in the signs she already obeys on the road.
options.viewport: Phone. Full-blue header plate with the hurricane glyph and 'StormCard'. A white sign panel reading 'ZONE B' in highway lettering, then three arrow plates, one per shelter, each with miles and a pet glyph.
options.risk: The most familiar route for public-safety apps; can feel like a government form.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: Carbon-copy airline ticket coupons and baggage tags (the Miami-Port-au-Prince route)
options.thesis: Her plan as a ticket wallet: each step is a coupon she tears off, nothing disappears.
options.viewport: Phone. Stacked coupon stubs: Language, Place, Household, then the Card coupon with zone and shelters printed in carbon fields.
options.case: Fuses well: the diaspora knows ticket coupons and the step-by-step flow is clear; loses on audience identification for a hurricane moment.
options.risk: Travel metaphor can confuse 'going to a shelter' with 'taking a trip'.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.case: Fuses poorly: shelters are not stations and a dark ground hurts older eyes in daylight.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.case: Declined: strobing and data density are hostile to a stressed 74-year-old.
options.kept: Total contrast commitment, no grey text.

options.label: Japanese High-Density Web
options.case: Declined: tiny type fails the large-type requirement.
options.kept: Header tabs on every section with a strict hairline border system.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean public-safety app (FEMA / county alert app), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Phone. White header, zone pill, three shelter list rows with chevrons, a blue primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every government app by design.
